extracted.intended_audience: research community, DOE stakeholders, potential EFRC applicants and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: A Department of Energy press release announcing awards to Energy Frontier Research Centers (EFRCs), describing program goals, eligible team/institution types, research topic areas, award durations, and selection process. Useful as guidance for understanding EFRC expectations and priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: fundamental/basic research to accelerate energy technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: EFRCs 'perform basic research that accelerates ground-breaking scientific advances underlying energy technologies.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since 2009, EFRCs have brought together teams to generate foundational knowledge to enable future energy technologies and national priorities (e.g., microelectronics, quantum information science). The centers are intended to advance the basic science that underpins DOE-relevant technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team composition and diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects must 'bring together diverse, world-class teams of scientists' and 'multidisciplinary scientific teams' to address the research challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams include investigators from universities, national laboratories, and partner institutions. The centers convene world-class, diverse participants to leverage complementary expertise across institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop new tools and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: EFRCs are expected to 'develop powerful new tools for characterizing, understanding, modeling, and manipulating matter.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on generating enabling tools and capabilities (experimental, computational, theoretical) that advance the understanding and control of materials and processes relevant to energy technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce development and training
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Training the next-generation scientific workforce by attracting talented students passionate about energy science' is an explicit program objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers should include activities that educate and attract students and early-career researchers, building capacity for future energy science and technology efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical and technical focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards support fundamental research in specified topical areas including microelectronics, quantum information science, advanced manufacturing (including polymers and co-design of materials and processes), and environmental management (e.g., nuclear waste tank management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement highlights focus on polymers, microelectronics fabrication science, quantum technologies, energy-efficient magnonics, quantum sensing, molecular quantum transduction, upcycling of plastics, and resilient grid materials—projects should align with these priority topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional leadership and partnership expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects are to be 'led by universities and national laboratories' and may include 'more than 65 additional partner institutions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership by a university or national lab and broad institutional partnerships are characteristic of selected centers; selected centers join an existing network of EFRCs (e.g., 33 existing centers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project duration and award types
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The projects, which can be up to four years in duration,' and the funding announcement supports 'three new and five continuing four-year awards and two two-year transition awards.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals/centers should plan for multi-year efforts (typically up to four years), while transition awards may be shorter (two years), reflecting different award categories and stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection mechanism and conditionality
rubrics_metrics.description: 'The projects were selected by competitive peer review under the DOE Funding Opportunity Announcement for Energy Frontier Research Centers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection for award negotiations is not a commitment to issue funding; DOE and applicants undergo negotiations and DOE may cancel negotiations or rescind selections for any reason prior to final award. Applicants should expect peer review and subsequent negotiation steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended impact: enable national priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers should 'generate knowledge to enable future energy technologies and other national priorities such as microelectronics and quantum information science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond scientific advances, projects are expected to have clear lines to enabling technologies and national strategic priorities identified by DOE.
